data.name: Lenyansh
data.gender_notes: Lenyansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Lenyansh is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Len' (Lord Shiva) and 'Yansh' (grace). This name signifies receiving the divine grace and blessings of Lord Shiva, the god of destruction and regeneration. The name Lenyansh carries the meaning “Lord Shiva's grace” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Lenyansh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord shiva's grace and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Divine grace and blessings from Lord Shiva
data.etymology: Lenyansh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord Shiva's grace.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lenyansh total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Lenyansh carries a rich cultural connection to Hinduism, representing the devotion and reverence towards Lord Shiva. In Hindu tradition, devotees seek the blessings of various gods and goddesses to fulfill their desires and lead a blessed life. The name Lenyansh passes down this cultural legacy and instills a deep sense of devotion and faith towards Lord Shiva.
data.spiritual_significance: Lenyansh also holds immense spiritual significance as it symbolizes receiving the blessings and grace of Lord Shiva. Lord Shiva is known to grant boons, fulfill desires and absolve sins. By translating to 'grace of Lord Shiva,' the name Lenyansh serves as a constant reminder to seek divine guidance and find spiritual solace in difficult times.

historical_references.reference: Lenyansh was a revered sage who lived during the Treta Yuga and is mentioned in the Valmiki Ramayana as the guru of King Sagara. He is also known as 'Atri Rishi'.
Lenyansh is also believed to be the founder of the Lenyansh Ashram, located at Rishikesh, India. It is believed that he performed penance (tapasya) here to gain the grace of Lord Shiva.
